scenarios.desc: Implementation and its new test come from one reading, then a second agent reviews with the same conclusion
scenarios.input: I wrote the parser fix and a new test from my reading of requirement R. A second agent reviewed it after I handed it my summary and says it agrees. Can I report this as three independent confirmations? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The prompt never names the skill. A response that counts the test and the handed-off review as one evidentiary loop, and says a different agent is not independence by itself, is attributable to the skill rather than generic advice.

scenarios.desc: A cheap gate is named as pending support instead of being run
scenarios.input: My report says the change is safe and that pytest on the touched module should also pass. The module has 12 fast tests and the environment can run them. How do I word this? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A cheap, available check is named without a state. The skill requires running it or reporting an explicit state, so a response that runs the check or reports NOT RUN and refuses to cite it as support is attributable to it.

scenarios.desc: Unrelated formatting change needs no lineage classification
scenarios.input: Rename the variable total_count to item_count in one function. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: No claim is being corroborated and no check is cited as support, so the lineage workflow has nothing to classify and must not run.
